1.why: Protected MFA endpoints resolve the account from the authenticated session via owner/verified rather than trusting a user-supplied identifier.

2.why: Identity codes are stored per session and TOTP/recovery codes are validated against the signed-in account, so a code is not shared across users.

3.why: Enabling MFA only sets account.mfa and does not invalidate, rotate, or delete existing sessions, so prior valid sessions remain usable.

4.why: The OTP secret is stored as AES-GCM encrypted data and recovery codes are stored as peppered SHA-256 hashes rather than plaintext.

5.why: Random secrets, OTPs, recovery codes, session identifiers, and CSRF tokens are generated using crypto.getRandomValues or crypto.subtle.generateKey.

6.why: The session identifier is placed only in an HttpOnly cookie and no localStorage/sessionStorage is used, although OTP secrets and backup codes are exposed in the client-side UI and console.

7.why: Server-side checks validate email format and length, six-digit OTP values, and recovery-code format, although no phone input is present.

8.why: Dynamic values such as codes and messages are rendered with textContent rather than inserted as raw HTML, preventing injected markup from executing.

9.why: The application does not issue redirects or Location headers, but it also does not implement an explicit redirect allow-list.

10.why: Responses include CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options DENY, and CSP frame-ancestors protection.

11.why: The mfa_session cookie is set with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict attributes.

12.why: Client-side code logs the provisioning secret, provisioning URI, identity OTP, practice codes, and backup recovery codes to the console and visible log area.

13.why: Identity codes have an expiry and used flag, TOTP counters are recorded to prevent reuse, and recovery codes are deleted after successful verification.

14.why: Login, identity verification, authenticator confirmation, and recovery verification all lock further attempts after repeated failures.

15.why: Login deletes the old session and creates a new session identifier, sessions enforce idle and absolute timeouts, and logout deletes the session.
